entities.summary: Spanish Baroque literature is the literature written in Spain during the Baroque, which occurred during the 17th century in which prose writers such as Baltasar Gracián and Francisco de Quevedo, playwrights such as Lope de Vega, Tirso de Molina, Calderón de la Barca and Juan Ruiz de Alarcón, or the poetic production of the aforementioned Francisco de Quevedo, Lope de Vega and Luis de Góngora reached their zenith. Spanish Baroque literature is a period of writing which begins approximately with the first works of Luis de Góngora and Lope de Vega, in the 1580s, and continues into the late 17th century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Spanish Baroque literature had a significant regional impact on the development of Western literature, with notable writers such as Lope de Vega and Luis de Góngora contributing to the works of later literary movements. The period's emphasis on emotional intensity and complex moral themes also influenced the Romantic movement.
